links.reason: The passage recommends extracting code into a project, creating fixtures, writing tests, and deploying the data pipeline, but it does not clearly describe regularly executing the complete data, training, and model pipeline before production.

links.label: Distinct ML monitoring domain
links.description: Treat monitoring of model behavior and impact as a specialized operational discipline distinct from general software monitoring.
links.reason: The passage distinguishes operational and ML issues and discusses monitoring model inputs, predictions, usage, drift, and performance, but does not explicitly establish ML monitoring as a specialized discipline distinct from general software monitoring.

links.label: Parallel stateless prediction pipelines
links.description: Multiple stateless prediction pipelines scale horizontally to accommodate load.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that multiple parallel pipelines can be created to accommodate load because the ML models are stateless.

links.label: Time- and event-triggered training
links.description: Schedulers, calendar events, messages, monitoring events, or data and code changes initiate training.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that automated training can be triggered by calendar events, messages, monitoring events, and changes to data or code, and describes retraining when new data becomes available.

links.label: Automated end-to-end pipeline testing
links.description: The complete data, training, and model pipeline is regularly executed and checked before production.
links.reason: The passage describes CI/CD tests that execute and validate pipeline components, integration, training, data, and prediction services before deployment to production.

links.label: Experiment lifecycle tracking platform
links.description: A platform records experiments and manages the machine-learning lifecycle between development and deployment.
links.reason: The passage discusses tracking ML experiments, reproducibility, and the development-to-deployment lifecycle, but it does not clearly describe or adopt a platform that records and manages this lifecycle.

links.label: Experiment lifecycle tracking platform
links.description: A platform records experiments and manages the machine-learning lifecycle between development and deployment.
links.reason: The passage describes experiment tracking and MLOps processes that record training information across runs and manage model development, packaging, validation, deployment, and monitoring.

links.label: Web-service model deployment
links.description: Hosting trained models behind web-service interfaces in cloud or local environments.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that trained models are deployed as web services in cloud or local environments and describes the required service deployment components.

links.label: Continuous delivery pipeline
links.description: Model releases are automatically delivered through a continuous delivery process.
links.reason: The passage states that the model has its own independent release cycle, but does not describe automatic delivery through a continuous delivery pipeline.

links.label: Notebook production pipeline
links.description: Using notebooks as the production pipeline was explicitly rejected.
links.reason: The passage adopts a notebook as an end-to-end production pipeline, but does not support the claim that this approach was explicitly rejected.

links.label: Offline batch training
links.description: Training runs as an offline process rather than during prediction requests.
links.reason: The passage explicitly defines offline (batch/static) learning as training the model on already collected data, separate from production prediction.

links.label: Manual deep-learning hyperparameter tuning
links.description: Manually exploring deep-learning hyperparameters without automated search.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes setting hyperparameters by hand and optimizing them through trial and error, while noting that this is impractical for deep learning.

links.label: Notebook-based prototyping
links.description: Data scientists prototype with notebooks despite an enterprise-provided platform.
links.reason: The passage explicitly discusses when data scientists should use or move away from Jupyter notebooks, including their use for prototyping despite broader engineering concerns.

links.label: Containerized prediction microservice
links.description: A prediction model is packaged and deployed as a containerized microservice.
links.reason: The passage discusses deploying ML pipelines, APIs, and CI/CD automation but does not describe or consider packaging the prediction model as a containerized microservice.

links.label: Continuous integration pipeline
links.description: An adopted continuous-integration pipeline supports implementation testing and delivery.
links.reason: The passage explicitly recommends setting up a CI/CD system to automatically test and deploy new ML pipeline implementations.

links.label: Microservice architecture
links.description: Clearly separated product components are independently served as microservices.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes microservices as independently developed and customized components that are connected and orchestrated, supporting a microservice architecture.

links.label: Software-metrics-only monitoring
links.description: Rely exclusively on software metrics to monitor a production model.
links.reason: The passage explicitly rejects relying only on software metrics, stating that this approach is insufficient for monitoring a production model.

links.label: Active model performance monitoring
links.description: The source explicitly rejected active model-performance monitoring as the selected monitoring approach.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that level 0 lacks active performance monitoring, meaning this approach is not adopted and is effectively rejected.

links.label: Single-objective error minimization
links.description: Considering one error objective instead of broader operational criteria was rejected for model assessment.
links.reason: The passage rejects relying solely on error minimization, emphasizing broader criteria such as stability, ethics, fairness, explainability, user experience, and edge-case performance for ongoing model assessment.

links.label: Business-KPI-only monitoring
links.description: Wait exclusively for downstream product or business KPIs to monitor model behavior.
links.reason: The passage explicitly rejects relying only on downstream business KPIs, directly supporting the rejection of business-KPI-only monitoring.

links.label: Local-machine data access
links.description: Develop by accessing protected data directly from a local machine.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that local-machine data access was not allowed and was rejected in favor of secure VM-based access.

links.label: Direct underlying-data access
links.description: Allowing direct access to underlying data was explicitly rejected as an infrastructure access approach.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says organizations do not want too many users having direct access to the underlying data, indicating that this access approach is rejected.

links.label: Silent model failure
links.description: Harmful or incorrect predictions that appear operationally successful and evade ordinary outage detection.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes harmful or incorrect model predictions that return normally, evade outage detection, and are discovered only later through business impact.

links.label: Research-production numerical divergence
links.description: Dependency differences cause numerical calculations to differ between research and production.
links.reason: The passage describes dependency/language differences between research and production that can reduce model accuracy, but it does not specifically state numerical calculations diverge because of dependency differences.

links.label: Reliability gaps from insufficient testing
links.description: Insufficient testing leaves serious reliability holes and requires further productionization investment.
links.reason: The passage explicitly links low testing levels to serious reliability holes and, at slightly higher scores, the need for additional productionization investment.

links.label: Duplicated credential management
links.description: Maintain access credentials separately across notebooks.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes duplicated access-credential management across notebooks and the need to update each notebook when credentials change.

links.label: Reduced hyperparameter-search burden
links.description: Reduced data-scientist effort resulting from automated hyperparameter optimization.
links.reason: The passage states that automated HPO relieves data-science teams of intensive manual hyperparameter exploration and optimization, reducing their effort.

links.label: Permissive open-source licensing
links.description: Permit open-source technology selection only when licensing meets permissive organizational requirements.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that open-source software is allowed only when it has permissive licenses, directly matching the stated governance requirement.

links.label: Shared-transformation downstream improvement
links.description: Improving one canonical production transformation automatically improves dependent downstream pipelines.
links.reason: The passage describes feature transformations within a model-building pipeline but does not state that improving one canonical production transformation automatically improves dependent downstream pipelines.

links.label: Rigid resource-intensive processing
links.description: Experience rigid architecture and substantial resource consumption from traditional batch processing.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes the Hadoop-based batch process as rigid and very resource intensive.

links.label: Model version tracking
links.description: Versions and their publication dates are recorded for change management.
links.reason: The passage mentions multiple model versions for retraining and change-related automation, but does not state that versions or their publication dates are recorded.

links.label: User-defined dataset validation
links.description: Custom routines detect inconsistencies, incorrect associations, missing values, and other data errors.
links.reason: The passage states that MLOps performs data validation to eliminate false insights, but it does not specify user-defined routines or the listed error types such as inconsistencies, incorrect associations, or missing values.
